To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the design of audio segmentation algorithms and feature extraction should be done dependently on the characteristics of the music genre, (b) the design of music structural segmentation systems should account for the contextual information of music corpora to be segmented, (c) the use of harmonic-percussing source separation in audio feature extraction can improve music structural segmentation performance, (d) the use of novelty- and homogeneity-based audio segmentation algorithms can improve music structural performance for genres that lack repetition patterns,

(1) different music genres have different structural patterns and different features capture these patterns in different ways; (2) the design of audio-based features and segmentation algorithms should consider the music corpora and their characteristics; (3) a harmonic-percussing source separation technique brings significant improvement to music segmentation; and (4) novelty- and homogeneity-based segmentation and timbre features outperform the investigated alternatives for Jingju music segmentation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the music structure is a very complex and subjective phenomenon and it is hard to be captured by a single feature and a single structural hypothesis.
there is no best segmentation method, and no best feature, but there is an optimal segmentation algorithm and an optimal feature for each specific genre.
there is no best feature, best hypothesis, best algorithm, or best annotation principle that can be applied to all music corpora.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel music segmentation algorithm that can be used to segment Jingju music, and that this algorithm is better than other existing segmentation algorithms in the literature.
the structural patterns of music genres are not universal, but they are genre-specific, and that they are not only determined by the musical content, but also by the cultural context.
the design of a music segmentation system should take into account the characteristics of the music genre, the music structure, and the audio features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the segmentation of music is a highly context-dependent task.
a music genre should be treated as a distinct case when designing a music structural segmentation system.
a segmentation system that is trained on a Western music corpus cannot be directly used for other music genres.
